description: Step-by-step derivation of c_q ≈ 9.0926 at the substrate parameter q_0 from first principles (categorical action + Frobenius pairing + nonabelian Stokes).  All intermediate steps are AXIOM, MATHLIB_CITED, or DERIVED — no SCRIPT_CITED frontier.  This is a fully-trusted chain modulo the three AXIOM entrypoints.

steps.name: q-connection A_q via categorical action
steps.operation: The q-deformed connection on the state bundle is the categorical image A_q := q^{-1} A + ℏ_q · ι_ξ A · Θ where ℏ_q = 1 − q^{-1} and Θ is the contact 1-form (Reeb dual).
steps.output_value: A_q = q^{-1} A + ℏ_q · ι_ξ A · Θ
steps.notes: Categorical action of B_n on V^{⊗n} via the R-matrix induces a q-deformation of parallel transport; the splitting horizontal + vertical comes from the Reeb foliation.  See content/quantum-universes/q-connection.md (ex:q-connection).

steps.name: Reeb decomposition A = A_H + (ι_ξ A) · Θ
steps.operation: The Frobenius pairing identifies the dual of the contact form Θ as the Reeb vector field ξ; this gives the canonical splitting A = A_H + (ι_ξ A) · Θ where A_H is horizontal.
steps.output_value: A_H ⊕ ⟨ι_ξ A, Θ⟩ — Frobenius-dual splitting of A
steps.notes: Frobenius theorem (Mathlib: `Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.ContactGeometry.Frobenius`) underwrites the integrability of the horizontal distribution ker(Θ); the vertical complement is generated by ξ.

steps.name: Nonabelian Stokes consistency of A_q on each cell
steps.operation: The holonomy of A_q around an elementary cell satisfies the nonabelian Stokes identity hol(∂cell) = exp(∫_cell F_q), with F_q := dA_q + A_q ∧ A_q the q-curvature.  This pins the horizontal vs vertical coupling weights to q^{-1} and ℏ_q respectively (no other splitting is consistent).
steps.notes: Nonabelian Stokes is the integrability obstruction; in the QOU framework it forces the q-connection coefficients to be exactly (q^{-1}, ℏ_q).  CLAUDE.md §7 lists this as one of the seven first-principles entrypoints.

steps.name: Contact-affine ratio c_q := q^{-1} / ℏ_q
steps.operation: Define c_q as the ratio of horizontal to vertical coupling weights: c_q := q^{-1} / ℏ_q.  Algebraically: c_q = q^{-1} / (1 − q^{-1}) = 1 / (q − 1).
steps.notes: Pure algebra: q^{-1}/(1 − q^{-1}) · (q/q) = 1/(q − 1).  The DERIVED trust basis records that this step has no new axiom input; it is a one-line manipulation of the previous step.

steps.name: Evaluate c_q at q_0 = 1.1099785955573347
steps.notes: COMPUTATIONAL leaf — bare arithmetic.  Matches the chapter's stated c ≈ 9.12 (rounded) in natural Reeb-step units.  This is NOT the SI 299792458 m/s; recovering the SI value requires the unit conversion via Planck time (see information-speed-of-light.md §Consistency).
